From: Maya Liu <maya.liu@finstack.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: concurrency and streaming needs

Thanks for the call this morning, Dylan — helpful overview. A few clarifications from our side so we can scope the pilot: 

- Target latency: 95th percentile under 400ms for short prompt/response pairs (~<256 tokens). For streaming endpoints, we need first-byte under 150ms and steady inter-token delivery.
- Peak concurrency: we expect bursts to 120 parallel requests for short calls across our EU+US regions; typical sustained concurrency will be ~45.
- Connection model: we prefer long-lived websocket connections with multiplexing; connection churn should be minimized.

We also have standard security questions (SOC2, ingress IP ranges) — happy to send a short packet after you confirm the pilot terms.

Next steps: please send a proposed pilot plan and an initial rate/quotas sheet we can review with our infra team.

—Maya
Senior Engineering Manager, FinStack
ops@finstack.com

Maya — thanks, that's very clear and exactly what we needed. Attached is a lightweight pilot worksheet (redwood-conn-pilot-worksheet.xlsx) to capture traffic shape and endpoints, plus an initial ratecard PDF (redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf).

Quick summary of what we'll propose internally:
- Pilot duration: 4 weeks (1 week ramp, 2 weeks steady, 1 week wrap + eval)
- Pilot quotas: baseline = 50 sustained concurrent requests, burst = 140 for 10m windows (we can tighten burst window if needed)
- Per-route SLOs: 95p latency target = 350–400ms for non-streaming; streaming first-byte under 120–150ms, token cadence configurable via stream buffer size
- Connection guidance: recommend websocket multiplexing with 8 logical channels per connection (configurable). If you prefer HTTP/2 long-poll, we can align but websocket gives the best steady-state latency for your use case

Action items for FinStack: fill the worksheet with sample qps/seq_len distribution + list of top 10 prompt types.
Action items for Redwood (Grace + Stephanie): produce a short runbook with quota/proxy settings and a recommended client backoff strategy, plus a one-page security evidence packet.

Cc'ing Grace for the pilot runbook and Stephanie for quota/price details. I'll follow up Monday with a one-page SLO matrix and suggested routing policy (US primary, EU fallback) so your EU traffic stays local when possible.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Looping back with technical notes to include in the runbook. Draft below — please review and edit before we send to Maya.

--- draft runbook excerpt ---
Pilot connection & concurrency plan (FinStack):
- Client model: persistent websocket with multiplexing (8 channels/conn). If FinStack wants fewer channels we can reduce; capacity calculations baked below.
- Tokenization: average response length estimated 120 tokens; avg prompt 40 tokens -> per-request token avg = 160.
- Throughput sizing: steady qps target based on 45 sustained concurrency and mean latency 250ms => ~180 QPS aggregate. Burst headroom to 140 conc for 10m windows => ~560 QPS short bursts.
- KV cache and prefix caching: enable prefix cache for top-10 prompts to reduce token spend and latency for repeated requests.
- Connection pooling & proxy: Recommend client open 12 websocket connections per region behind a load-balanced NAT to preserve connection reuse when clients are mobile. Each connection supports multiplexing; keep-alive 60s.
- Backoff & retry guidance: linear backoff with jitter; retry only idempotent requests (we'll add a request-id header).

Quota proposal (initial, pilot):
- baseline concurrency 50 (sustained), burst to 140 for 10 minutes, per-minute token cap 1.2M tokens.
- If FinStack exceeds burst 3 times in a 24h window, we auto-escalate to review and can offer temporary burst credits.

Operational hooks:
- Streaming SLO: first-byte <= 150ms 95p, inter-token median cadence <= 30ms for short responses.
- Observability: we'll grant FinStack a read-only dashboard with per-route 95p latency and connection occupancy.
--- end draft ---

Stephanie — can you put numbers for estimated GPU footprint (vCPU/GPU slots) and approximate cost delta for the pilot quotas above? I want to include a conservative cost estimate in the email to FinStack.

Grace
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Liu <maya.liu@finstack.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed pilot quotas & rate limits for FinStack (FS-2026-0911)

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call and the quick follow. We're aligned on latency and connection model. Below is a conservative quota sheet for the 4-week pilot. I've attached the ratecard PDF for detailed pricing.

Proposed pilot quotas (effective immediately for pilot):
- Sustained concurrency: 50 concurrent requests (per-region)
- Burst concurrency: 140 concurrent requests (global) for up to 10 continuous minutes, can be used 4x/day before requiring a manual review
- Connection limits: recommend 12 websocket connections per client IP per region, multiplex 8 channels per connection (configurable)
- Rate limits: 120k tokens/minute aggregate for pilot (global); per-route soft limit at 60k tokens/minute
- Backpressure behavior: when hitting soft limits, we return 429 with Retry-After and a short binary-exponential backoff suggestion; when hitting hard limits, we return 509 + short failure message and log for escalation

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf (pricing scenarios + pilot credit options).

Next steps:
1) Maya: confirm worksheet completion and any adjustments to burst windows (you mentioned EU regulatory traffic separation).
2) FinStack infra: send sample traffic CSV (timestamp, seq_len, prompt_type) — we'll ingest into the pilot sizing workbook.
3) We'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for the pilot next week to walk the runbook and security packet.

Happy to jump on a call if you want to tighten any of the numbers before we lock the pilot.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Product Ops — Redwood Optimize
